SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MAY 11, 2015 - CITY HALL -
7:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
MAY 11, 2015 IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Alex Kim, First Evangelical Church of Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Brownie Troop #1043.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair George Ray
  Mayor/Chair Carol Chen

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Presentations were made as follows:

  Chuan-Ling Lie (95th Birthday)

  Ophelia Lara (Gahr High School Girls Varsity Wrestler)

  American Red Cross (Certificate of Recognition to the City Council)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Julie Schwartz, Manager of the Saturday Morning Farmers Market in Cerritos,
  introduced herself to the community.

  Morris Satki, resident, expressed concerns regarding the parkway tree near his
  residence.

  motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency
  Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be removed from the
  Consent Calendar and considered separately.

  May 11, 2015 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register of
  Demands dated May 11, 2015 in the total amount of $6,497,686.95 (COUNCIL). The
  motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of an appeal of a decision of the Cerritos Property
  Preservation Commission denying a request to remove one parkway tree
  adjacent to the property located at 18509 Bainbrook Court, Cerritos, California,
  90703 (APN 7023-009-014) – Case No. TR 2015-01 (COUNCIL).

  Appeal to City Council PPC - 2015-01

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Karla McIrney, representing the appellant, submitted pictures for the record, and
  expressed concerns regarding the parkway tree in front of the subject property.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.
 City of Cerritos  May 11, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Uphold the Property Preservation Commission’s determination denying the property
  owner’s request to remove the parkway tree located adjacent to the 18509 Bainbrook
  Court residence, in accordance with the City’s Tree Ordinance, and
  2. Inform the property owner of the City Council’s determination regarding the removal
  of said parkway tree (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for street improvements on
  Bechard Avenue Alley, Palm Street, Park Street and Parkside Avenue, Project No.
  13053, Bid No. 1206-15 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Hal Arbogast, Director of Public Works.  A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $382,225.00 for Street Improvements on Bechard
  Avenue Alley, Palm Street, Park Street and Parkside Avenue, Project No. 13053,
  Bid No. 1206-15, to Sequel Contractors and reject all other bids, and

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

10B1. Review and consideration of State legislation to oppose Assembly Bill 45 (Mullin)
  which would require each jurisdiction that provides residential collection and
  disposal of solid waste to increase the collection and diversion of household
  hazardous waste in its service area (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  (Item 10B1 continued on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  May 11, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B1. (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Concur with the Los Angeles County Sanitation District, the Los Angeles County
  Solid Waste Management Committee/Integrated Waste Management Task Force, a
  number of other cities and counties throughout the State, and waste associations
  to oppose AB 45, and
  2. Prepare letters of opposition to be sent to Speaker Pro Tem Mullin, Assembly
  Appropriations Committee, Senator Mendoza, Assemblymember Garcia, Los
  Angeles County Board of Supervisors, Los Angeles County Sanitation District, Los
  Angeles County Solid Waste Management Committee/Integrated Waste
  Management Task Force, League of California Cities (Los Angeles Division),
  Gateway Cities Council of Governments, California Contract Cities, Independent
  Cities Association, and Gonsalves and Son (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Pulido, and Solanki, Mayor Pro

  The City Council recessed to Closed Session to consider item 12A.

12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6. (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci, Patricia Leyva

  Report from Closed Session:

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss item 12A on the Closed Session

  Chamber. The City Attorney reported that the City Council met in Closed Session to
  discuss item 12A on the agenda as related to labor negotiations. Direction was
  provided to the negotiators and there was no further action to report (COUNCIL).

(Minutes continue on the next page)
